decisions.statement: A call between backticks in a literal was marked as a call and is judged as one.
The first word after `akasha` names a level or nothing there is judged.
A word names a level where the level before it and that word join to a slug.
A word after a command is an argument rather than a level.
A word carrying anything but lowercase letters, digits and hyphens ends the read.
A call ending on a namespace is a listing rather than a fault.
The refusal names the deepest level the call reached.
The line named is the line the literal is on.
A call spelled with no backticks around it is not judged.
A call inside a finding is not judged, a finding holding what was said when it was said.
A finding is where the tree holds a past state rather than what is true now.
A call whose first word names no level is not judged.
A level whose name is not its own slug is no first word here.
A call built as the code runs is not judged here.
A word this rule takes for an argument is not judged against the arguments.

definition: the rule refusing a call marked in a literal whose word under a namespace names no level there
